02 · Fix one — hours
The #1 complaint, solved first

“Is it open today?” is now the site's job one

Before
  • Hours listed with a “pm” typo (8:30 pm–3:00 pm) — and no honest word about cruise-day reality.
  • Visitors walked over and found an empty lot.

“We went yesterday (Friday June 10th) and it wasn't open, just a big empty parking lot.”

— visitor review of the market (audit, recurring theme)
After
  • A live open/closed status, computed in Cayman time, shown in the header of every page and answered in the first screen of the homepage.
  • The honest caveat, stated plainly: vendors follow the ships — fullest on cruise days, call ahead if your day depends on it.
  • Correct hours everywhere: Mon–Fri 8:30am–3:00pm, holiday and severe-weather closures included.

The homepage answers the two big questions before a single scroll — live status, hours, cruise-day reality, location, phone.

03 · Fix two — location

An authored walking map — tender landing to tent — with step-by-step directions and a Google Maps link.

One market, one address

From three addresses to one findable tent

Before
  • “N Church St” in the header, “Boilers Road & South Church Street” in the body, “next to Dairy Queen” in a pop-up — while the market had actually moved behind Parliament.
  • Google Maps still pins the old location; reviewers reported literally failing to find the market.
After
  • One canonical location — the tent behind Parliament, off Seafarers Way — stated identically on every page.
  • A drawn walking map from the cruise tender landing (≈5 minutes, flat), because that's the walk 9 in 10 visitors actually make.
  • Built to move: every location mention reads from one editable module in the code — if Parliament expansion forces a relocation, it's a one-line update.
Why it matters

The market may be forced to relocate again. The old site never recovered from its last move — the new one is designed to survive the next.

04 · Fix three — the story
The differentiator, finally on the page

Buy it from the hands that made it

Before
  • Not a single vendor named or pictured. The market's real advantage — meeting the maker — was invisible online.
  • Meanwhile “dollar-store souvenirs” criticism went unanswered.
After
  • Artisan profiles — Rosemary, Janet, Ruth Bodden, Franklin, Cayman Drift — each paired with a real visitor quote naming them.
  • A heritage section: Silver Thatch (the national tree), Caymanite (found nowhere else on Earth), black coral — the story that separates this tent from every souvenir shop on the strip.
  • Honest expectation-setting: “small on purpose”, stall count follows the ships — so nobody arrives expecting a mall.
Why it matters

No competitor owns “authentic, meet-the-maker Caymanian craft at the cruise port.” This is the market's open lane, and now its website drives in it.

Every profile carries a genuine Tripadvisor quote — replacing the old site's tour-company reviews.

05 · The design system
Why it looks the way it looks

The brand is cut from the stone

Instead of a generic island template, every visual decision is derived from things that exist only here:

  • The Caymanite strata motif. The layered bands in the logo and section dividers are the stone's own natural stripes — a mark no other market could truthfully wear.
  • A palette from the site's subjects: harbour teal, sand, Silver Thatch straw, Caymanite rust and brown — with one coral accent reserved for calls to action.
  • Type with craft in it: Bricolage Grotesque for display (hand-cut character) with Karla for reading comfort.
  • Illustrated, not faked: until real photography is shot, maker panels use authored craft patterns — never stock photos pretending to be the market.
Harbour deep
Sand
Thatch straw
Caymanite rust
Coral — CTAs only

The heritage pages give the crafts their history — depth the old single-page site had nowhere to put.

06 · Trust, search & phones
The invisible fixes

Built for a visitor holding a phone on a ship

Before
  • Casino spam and another company's reviews eroding trust in an official attraction.
  • No structured data — third-party listings (with wrong info) outranked the official site.
  • A desktop-era layout for an audience that arrives almost entirely on phones.
After
  • Only genuine market testimonials, quoted verbatim from Tripadvisor, naming real vendors.
  • Consistent name–address–phone on every page plus TouristAttraction structured data — the foundation for outranking stale listings and fixing the Google pin.
  • Mobile-first and fast: a single lightweight page, no heavy frameworks, WCAG AA contrast, keyboard and reduced-motion support — verified in a headless browser at phone and desktop sizes.

The core audience: a cruise passenger with 20 spare minutes and one bar of signal.

07 · What happens next
Staged rollout

Live now, sharper with each phase

  1. Confirm & correct (now)

    Five facts to verify with CINAA before the domain switch: the exact map pin, founding year, whether both phone numbers are live, the official logo, and the Saturday-opening rule. Claim the Google Business Profile and align every listing to the new site.

  2. Point craftmarket.ky here

    The site is a single static file — it can be hosted anywhere the domain points, with no rebuild. Swap in real photography of the makers as it's shot; every image slot is labelled for one-for-one replacement.

  3. Cruise-day calendar

    The open/closed logic lives in one function — wiring in the Port Authority ship schedule turns “is it open?” into “two ships in port today.”

Nine categories, every one Caymanian-made — the honest inventory, ready for photography.
